h: Leeds climbing, sorted from start to finish
p: Organising a party or a big group? Clip 'n Climb is a cracking choice, but it rewards a bit of organisation. Book the slot well ahead for weekends, and send all the parents a reminder to fill in the participation form online, because every climber needs one and parents or guardians must sign for under-18s. Ten families doing it at the desk on the day is a recipe for chaos.

Check the age guidance when you book, as there's usually a minimum age for climbers and supervision rules for younger children. Plan for a couple of hours in total, including arrival, harnessing and the safety briefing.

Once on the walls, the side-by-side races are always the big hit with groups. Pair up kids of similar sizes for fair races, and let the nervous ones try a low climb first. Water bottles, trainers and comfy clothes are all you need.

Leeds has loads to keep the fun going. Roundhay Park, in the north of the city, is a vast green space with lakes, woodland and gardens, plus Tropical World, home to butterflies, meerkats and reptiles under glass. Leeds City Museum, by Millennium Square, is free and full of curiosities, and Kirkstall Abbey, the striking ruins of a Cistercian abbey west of the centre, is a lovely spot for a picnic.
